chunks: And Zurārah ibn Aʿyan said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said:

“What Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made obligatory upon the servants was ten rakʿahs, and in them is recitation, and there is no doubt in them, meaning forgetfulness. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله added seven, and in them there is forgetfulness, and in them there is no recitation. So whoever doubts in the first two must repeat until he preserves it and is upon certainty; and whoever doubts in the last two should act upon assumption.”

key_terms.الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ: The last two rakʿahs of the prayer, in which one acts on assumption.
key_terms.الْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ: The first two rakʿahs of the prayer, in which doubt requires repetition.
key_terms.الْقِرَاءَةُ: The recitation required in the specified rakʿahs of the prayer.
key_terms.رَكَعَاتٍ: Units of salat being discussed as legally obligatory.
key_terms.سَهْوٌ: Forgetfulness or inadvertent error occurring during salat.
key_terms.وَهْمٌ: Doubt or uncertain estimation in prayer, explained here as forgetfulness.
key_terms.يَقِينٍ: Certainty, which is required regarding the first two rakʿahs.

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they doubt the number of rakʿahs in salat?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the distinction between the originally obligated rakʿahs and the rakʿahs later added by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in the daily salat. It establishes a legal ruling on doubt in prayer: doubt in the first two rakʿahs requires repetition until certainty is attained, while doubt in the last two is handled by acting on one’s predominant assumption.
